summary:
**Landsat** is an AI-powered agro-climatic intelligence web application designed to evaluate soil health and recommend optimal crops for any farmland on Earth.

Using **live GPS geolocation** or an interactive satellite map, Landsat pulls real-time agro-climatology data directly from **NASA POWER** and **MERRA-2** satellite systems. It measures key physical parameters, including root-zone soil wetness (`GWETROOT`), surface moisture (`GWETTOP`), soil temperature (`TS`), annual rainfall, solar irradiance, and atmospheric humidity.

From these parameters, the system diagnoses the soil profile using USDA-FAO pedology taxonomies—determining soil type (such as Alluvial Loam or Black Cotton Vertisol), drainage capacity, pH regime, and a fertility health score. It then cross-references this profile against a comprehensive matrix of 30+ crops (cereals, pulses, cash crops, oilseeds, and vegetables) to calculate dynamic 0–100% suitability scores, water requirements, sowing windows, and N-P-K fertilizer schedules.

Built for hands-free field use, Landsat features a **microphone voice assistant** (Web Speech API) with live audio frequency visualizers and speech synthesis narration, an animated hydrology soil strata cross-section, and a standalone architecture running seamlessly in any modern web browser.
